title: Deterministic Verification and a Single‑Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We present a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation per intent reused for both episodes), we produced N = 250 intent pairs with gpt-5-mini and evaluated two episodes per intent on a synthetic/emulation partition: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared-generation + 1 repair). Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired-bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. Important scope note (preregistered deviation disclosed here and in the Disclosure Statement): the preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed; the reported confirmatory estimand applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition run.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps), offering the prospect of rapid drafting of device CLI sequences and intent-driven automation. Stochastic generation, however, introduces operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, workflow-violation sequences, and vendor-CLI subtleties can produce unsafe or non-functional changes. Deterministic validators and bounded repair workflows (generate–verify–repair, GVR) are widely proposed to mitigate mechanically checkable defects while limiting trust in unconstrained LLM outputs [1]–[3].

Prior literature shows both that LLMs can produce usable draft configurations in controlled studies and that deterministic validators (header-space, model-checking, Batfish-style analyses) provide mechanized checks for many classes of errors, while also noting limitations for deeper semantic correctness and cross-vendor issues [1],[2],[4],[5]. Open empirical questions remain about the marginal benefit of interposing validators and limited repairs when modern LLM outputs already conform to validator encodings under constrained tasks.

Research question and contributions. We ask: When the same natural-language intent is realized by a single LLM-generated candidate and that candidate is either accepted (baseline) or passed through a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair (guarded), what is the paired difference in verifier-confirmed intent-satisfaction on a synthetic/emulation partition? Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired experiment under explicit shared_initial_candidate semantics that isolates the validator+repair marginal effect; (2) full numeric reconciliation and artifact-grounded reporting of execution accounting (N_pairs = 250; model_calls_used = 251; stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 250, repair = 1); and (3) quantitative results and uncertainty bounds showing a near-null marginal verifier-detected improvement for this constrained task bank, with archived artifacts enabling auditability.
sections.related_work:
Work on LLM-assisted network configuration and intent-driven management reports both promising draft-generation performance and persistent needs for verification [1],[2],[3]. Studies of LLM self-correction emphasize the importance of dependable external feedback or deterministic validators for reliable repair [2],[6]. Research on deterministic verification tools (Batfish, header-space and localized subspecification methods) documents mature methods for checking forwarding, reachability, and many local-policy properties; these tools are commonly proposed as validators in GVR pipelines [4],[5].

Generate–verify–repair and program-repair workflows in code and configuration domains show increased detection and conversion of mechanically checkable defects, but prior evaluations often operate on emulation-style benchmarks or single-case deployments and therefore leave sim-to-real external validity open [6],[7]. Security analyses of prompt-injection and retrieval-based threats underscore the continued need for filtering and validation layers in LLM-integrated pipelines, especially for NetOps workflows that can be targeted with malicious fragments [5].

This study differs by using a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics that measures only the marginal effect of deterministic validation and a single permitted repair on identical model outputs, and by publishing reconciliation statistics that map generation and repair stage counts to host-model call accounting.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1. The confirmatory design fixed N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one initial model generation per intent, reused for both baseline and guarded episodes), and the primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration froze the single-repair policy, exclusion rules, analysis tests (exact McNemar two-sided and paired-bootstrap percentile CIs), and a maximum model-call budget. Preregistration artifact SHA-256 is recorded in the Disclosure Statement.

Task bank and constraints. A deterministic task generator produced 250 constrained intent tasks (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5). Each task encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and a difficulty label (medium/hard/very_hard). Task families exercised workflow constraints such as make-before-break uplink switchover, paired-link atomic MTU changes, and safe access transfer patterns. All confirmatory episodes reported here were executed on the synthetic/emulation partition defined in the preregistration.

Model, pipeline, and repair policy. The declared model for initial generations was gpt-5-mini. For each intent we executed one shared initial generation call; the same candidate was evaluated in two episodes: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (submit candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5). If the guarded validator returned valid = false, the pipeline permitted at most one automated, template-constrained repair attempt (syntactic or ordering fixes) and re-submitted the repaired candidate. No multi-iteration repair or human escalation was permitted for confirmatory episodes.

Deterministic validator and scoring. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implements full_intent_constraint_validation: parsing CLI, counting parsed_command_count, checking required_sequence ordering, enforcing workflow constraints (group-activity and make-before-break), constructing a final_state snapshot and comparing it to the task expected_final_state. The validator returns a boolean valid flag and structured diagnostics (violation_codes, parsed counts, normalized_configuration), which determine the binary success/failure outcome used in the paired analysis.

Inclusion, contamination, and missingness rules. Preregistered exclusions removed outputs that failed vendor-parser deterministically preventing verification or that contained credential-like tokens/denylist hits. Contamination detectors flag instruction-like embedded tokens; flagged episodes were to be excluded from the primary analysis and handled in sensitivity treatments. For this confirmatory run no episodes were excluded or flagged.

Analysis plan. Primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1: exact two-sided McNemar on paired binary outcomes and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for guarded − baseline with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Sensitivity analyses were prespecified for missingness treatments and prompt-variant strata; those are not required here because missingness = 0.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250. Provider-call audit reconciled hosted_model_call_event_count = 251 (250 shared_initial_generation + 1 repair), recorded as model_calls_used = 251; stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}.

Primary binary outcomes and contingency. Validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency counts: n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair corresponds to the lone repair invocation that converted a baseline-fail into a guarded-pass; repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition = 1/250 = 0.4%.

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided p-value on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) is p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for the guarded − baseline paired difference (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] (0%–1.2 percentage points). Point estimate = +0.004 (0.4 percentage points).

Representative validator diagnostics. Passed episodes show parsed_command_count equal to required_command_count encoded by the task payload; for example a hard difficulty task (task-000003) exhibits parsed_command_count = 6, required_command_count = 6 and valid = true in both baseline and guarded episodes. Representative raw responses and normalized configurations are archived in the evidence bundle.

Missingness, exclusions, and contamination. No episodes were excluded under preregistered rules: complete_pairs = 250, and contamination detectors flagged zero confirmatory episodes. All reconciliation artifacts and CSV summaries referenced in this paper are archived in the evidence bundle named in the Disclosure Statement.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the near‑null marginal effect. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation tasks used here, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair was small. Initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249 of 250 cases; the one failing candidate was repaired by the single permitted template-driven repair. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) empirically bounds the maximum plausible verifier-detected improvement under these conditions.

Artifact-grounded reasons for the small gain. Three artifact-grounded factors explain the observation: (1) constrained task specification reduced ambiguity (task manifest encoded allowed_touched_fields and required_sequence); (2) the declared model produced syntactically well-formed and workflow-conformant sequences for the constrained intents; (3) the validator checks mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, final_state snapshot) and does not measure live protocol dynamics or emergent cross-device semantics.

Power and preregistration assumptions. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline pass ≈ 0.90 to detect a 15 percentage-point effect with ≈80% power and therefore motivated N_pairs = 250. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) materially exceeded that assumption, reducing statistical power to detect small absolute improvements; consequently, the bootstrap CI that bounds plausible effects under the run conditions is the most informative inferential output.

Threats to validity and scope. Internal validity: results depend on prompt templates, single-repair policy, and the strict shared_initial_candidate design (i.e., the study measures only marginal validator/repair effect on identical candidates). Construct validity: the deterministic validator assesses mechanically checkable correctness but not protocol-level behavioral correctness. External validity: findings apply only to the executed synthetic/emulation partition; the preregistered community and production-like partitions and sim-to-real confirmatory contrast were not executed and therefore remain untested. Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not exercised and remain open threats.

Operational implication (bounded). In tightly constrained emulation-style tasks with a capable LLM, a single-pass deterministic validator plus one template-driven repair may yield only marginal additional verifier-detected acceptance. This observation should not be generalized to broader operational contexts without additional evaluation across production heterogeneity, adversarial scenarios, multi-iteration repairs, or alternative validator scopes.
sections.conclusion: We ran a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to quantify the verifier-detected marginal effect of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. On N = 250 constrained synthetic intents with gpt-5-mini, initial candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the sole failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed and that these conclusions apply only to the synthetic/emulation partition. Broader evaluations (production topologies, adversarial threat models, multi-model comparison, and richer repair workflows) remain necessary to establish generality. All primary reconciliation facts reported here are directly reproducible from the archived evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and conducted pre-lock infrastructure development only; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and framework: declared model used for initial generations = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The guarded pipeline permitted at most one automated, template-constrained repair per episode as specified in the preregistration.

Preregistration and immutable master-prompt reference: preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). Immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.

Execution summary (concise): planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial-generation calls + 1 repair); stage_counts reconciled as {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}. These numeric reconciliation facts are reported in the paper body and are reproducible from the archived evidence bundle. The evidence bundle contains full execution and analysis manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and per-artifact hashes; file-level bookkeeping and the full hash manifest are archived in that bundle (manifest locator included in submission materials).

Executed confirmatory estimand and deviation disclosure: The preregistration specified multiple partitions including synthetic/emulation, community, and production-like (sim-to-real) confirmatory contrasts. Deviation disclosure (explicit): the preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed in this run; the executed confirmatory estimand reported in this manuscript is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated on the synthetic/emulation partition only (N_pairs = 250; shared_initial_candidate semantics). No manual post-lock modifications to reported numeric results were made.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions and the sim-to-real contrast were not executed.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, final_state snapshot) but did not measure live protocol-level behavioral correctness or emergent cross-device interactions.
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
